summary: FASE 8 — (1) Dashboard period filter↔AI Insights sync (2) IncomingOrders bukti-bayar badge + modal — ALL VERIFIED WORKING via live Playwright on production preview URL. Backend AI endpoint correctly accepts period={today,7d,14d,30d,1y,custom} + start/end. Frontend re-fetches /api/ai/insights on each period change and only after both custom dates are filled. Badge appears on 3/3 orders with payment_proof_url; modal opens with order#, customer, total, image, fullsize link, Tutup btn — all functional.

minor.issue: When response is served from cache (routes/ai_insights.py lines 137-143), the returned payload OMITS `_period_label`. Only freshly-generated responses include it (line 225). Frontend Dashboard.js line 577-578 has a fallback `data._period_label || data._period` which displays raw code ('today','7d','14d','1y','custom') in AI card subtitle instead of Indonesian labels ('hari ini','7 hari','14 hari','1 tahun', '<start> s/d <end>'). Fix: add `"_period_label": cached.get("data", {}).get("_period_label") or _compute_label(period, start, end)` to the cached return block, OR persist period_label inside cache_doc before storing.

issues: Subtitle shows raw period code (e.g. 'Cache (3 menit lalu) · today') instead of polished Indonesian label ('hari ini') when response is cached. Caused by backend not returning _period_label on cache hit — see backend minor issue above. Trivial 1-line fix.

action_items: Main agent: Add `_period_label` to the cached return block in /app/backend/routes/ai_insights.py (lines 137-143) so cached AI responses also return the Indonesian label. Suggested: persist `period_label` into cache_doc when first generating (line 209-218), then echo it back on cache hit.
critical_code_review_comments: Dashboard.js line 552-556 correctly guards custom-period fetch behind `if (period === 'custom' && (!customStart || !customEnd)) return;` — verified live: filling only start date triggers 0 calls, both → 1 call.

IncomingOrders.js line 250-266 conditional render `{order.payment_proof_url && ...}` + dual-state styling (green animate-pulse for `payment_proof_submitted=true`, amber for legacy URL-only) — verified live with 1 submitted + 2 legacy orders.
IncomingOrders.js line 255 prefix-resolution `src.startsWith('/api/') ? \`${API_URL}${url}\` : url` is correct — handles both relative (`/api/media/x`) and absolute proof URLs.

IncomingOrders.js WS handler line 157-163 listens for `payment_proof_submitted` event and updates order in-place — code path correct; not exercised live (would need POSTing to /api/orders/{id}/payment-proof to fire WS).
ai_insights.py: persisting period_label inside cache_doc is the cleanest fix for the cached-label bug — adds resilience without breaking cache invariants.
Dashboard.js fetchTab useCallback at line 741 has empty dep array — its closure captures `API` from module scope so OK, but ESLint may warn; consider including [API] for hygiene.

rca of the issue: AI Insights cached-response label bug RCA: In /app/backend/routes/ai_insights.py, the cache write at lines 209-218 stores `data` (raw LLM JSON) but does NOT persist `period_label`. On cache hit (lines 137-143), the spread `**cached.get('data', {})` only includes the LLM-generated keys + `_cached/_period/_generated_at/_cache_age_minutes` — `_period_label` is missing. Frontend shows raw `_period` value ('today','7d','custom') instead of Indonesian label. Mitigation: either (A) add `period_label` to cache_doc payload before upsert, then echo it on cache hit, OR (B) recompute period_label inside the cache-hit branch using the same days_map+label_map logic. Option A is preferred (single source of truth, handles custom date range with original start/end stored). Reproduction: GET /api/ai/insights?period=today twice → first response has _period_label='hari ini', second cached response is missing the field.
